ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that in $\triangle ABC$, $D$ and $E$ are the midpoints of $AB$ and $AC$, respectively. Connect $DE$ and extend it to $F$ such that $EF=DE$. Connect $CF$. If $\angle B=45^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle F$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since point E is the midpoint of AC, and point D is the midpoint of AB, \\
therefore $DE \parallel BC$ and $BC=2DE$. \\
Since EF=DE, \\
therefore $DF=2DE$, \\
therefore $DF=BC$, \\
therefore quadrilateral BCFD is a parallelogram, \\
therefore $\angle F=\angle B=45^\circ$. \\
Hence, the answer is: $\boxed{45^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is triangle ABC, with A above, B at the lower left, and C at the lower right. Point D is marked on side AB, point E is marked on side AC, and line segment DE is approximately horizontal; DE continues to extend rightward from E to point F, and EF is represented with a dashed line. Point C and F are connected with a dashed line. In the figure, BC is the base of the triangle, and DF is in the same direction as BC. Reasoning: It is known that D and E are respectively the midpoints of AB and AC. By the triangle midline theorem, DE ∥ BC, and DE = BC/2. Also because D, E, F are collinear, and EF = DE, therefore DF = DE + EF = 2DE = BC; at the same time DF ∥ BC. Thus in quadrilateral BCFD, one pair of opposite sides BC and DF are parallel and equal, therefore BCFD is a parallelogram. The opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal, so ∠F = ∠B. It is known that ∠B = 45°, therefore ∠F = 45°.
